How the children give the parent, by the supplied proof:

- Hence ζ(x)(w) = Σ_i (−1)^i Db(x)(w_i)·θ(Fin.cons (G x) (i.removeNth w)). This gives ‖ζ(x)‖ ≤ (m+1)·sup‖Db‖·‖θ‖·‖ι‖, and also ‖η(x)‖ ≤ sup|b|·‖θ‖·‖ι‖.

subproblems.title: Jacobi's trace identity: Σ_i det(u with column i replaced by A u_i) = tr(A)·det(u) (parent fact F3)
subproblems.statement: Let n ∈ ℕ, let A : ℝⁿ → ℝⁿ be ℝ-linear (ℝⁿ = Euclid n = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)), and let u : Fin n → ℝⁿ. For v : Fin n → ℝⁿ write D(v) := det(Matrix.of fun k j => v j k), the determinant of the n×n matrix whose j-th column is v j. Then Σ_{i ∈ Fin n} D(Function.update u i (A(u i))) = tr(A)·D(u), where tr(A) = LinearMap.trace ℝ ℝⁿ A.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (A : Euclid n →ₗ[ℝ] Euclid n) (u : Fin n → Euclid n), ∑ i : Fin n, Matrix.det (Matrix.of fun k j => Function.update u i (A (u i)) j k) = LinearMap.trace ℝ (Euclid n) A * Matrix.det (Matrix.of fun k j => u j k)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: the selected parent's proof (node root.dimension_reduction_results-a1.moving_blowups-a1.foundations-a1.divergence_form-a1), fact (F3) (Jacobi), with every step written out. Reuse: this child is the comparator-accepted theorem Submission.cmr_df_det_update_sum_trace of DAG node root.compactness_of_minimizing_currents-a1.mass_representation-a1.divergence_form-a1.jacobi_trace-a1 (candidate e4813e59). It is reused with its byte-identical frozen type, and the reviewed proof of that node is reproduced below. Step 5 corrects one phrase of the parent's (F3) (see there).

Notation.
- ℝⁿ := Euclid n = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n). e'_j := EuclideanSpace.single j 1 (j ∈ Fin n) is the standard basis. e := (EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin n) ℝ).toBasis is the same basis as a Module.Basis, so e j = e'_j and e.repr x k = x k.
- For v : Fin n → ℝⁿ, D(v) := det(Matrix.of fun k j => v j k). This is the determinant of the n×n matrix whose j-th column is v j.
- For i ∈ Fin n and v : Fin n → ℝⁿ, v⁽ⁱ⁾ := Function.update v i (A(v i)), i.e. v with its i-th entry replaced by A(v i).
- Φ(v) := Σ_{i ∈ Fin n} D(v⁽ⁱ⁾). We must show Φ(u) = tr(A)·D(u), where tr(A) = LinearMap.trace ℝ ℝⁿ A.

1. (D is the determinant of the standard basis.) For v : Fin n → ℝⁿ the matrix of the family v in the basis e is e.toMatrix v k j = e.repr(v j) k = v j k (Module.Basis.toMatrix_apply). By Module.Basis.det_apply, e.det v = det(e.toMatrix v) = D(v). So D = e.det is an alternating n-linear form on ℝⁿ, and D(e') = e.det e = 1 (Module.Basis.det_self).

2. (Φ is n-linear.) Fix i. For j ∈ Fin n put f_{i,j} := A if j = i, and f_{i,j} := id otherwise. Then v⁽ⁱ⁾ = (j ↦ f_{i,j}(v j)). So v ↦ D(v⁽ⁱ⁾) is the multilinear map e.det with the linear map f_{i,j} applied in slot j (MultilinearMap.compLinearMap), and it is n-linear. A finite sum of n-linear maps is n-linear, so Φ is n-linear.

3. (Φ is alternating.) Let v : Fin n → ℝⁿ and j ≠ l with v j = v l. We show Φ(v) = 0.
 (a) Let i ∉ {j, l}. Then v⁽ⁱ⁾ agrees with v at positions j and l, so it has the equal entries v j = v l at two distinct positions. Since D is alternating, D(v⁽ⁱ⁾) = 0.
 (b) Let σ := Equiv.swap j l. Then v⁽ˡ⁾ = v⁽ʲ⁾ ∘ σ. We check each position.
  - Position j: (v⁽ʲ⁾ ∘ σ)(j) = v⁽ʲ⁾(l) = v l, because l ≠ j. Also v⁽ˡ⁾(j) = v j, because j ≠ l. These agree since v j = v l.
  - Position l: (v⁽ʲ⁾ ∘ σ)(l) = v⁽ʲ⁾(j) = A(v j) = A(v l) = v⁽ˡ⁾(l).
  - Any other position k: both sides equal v k.
 (c) D is alternating, so D(v⁽ʲ⁾ ∘ σ) = −D(v⁽ʲ⁾) (AlternatingMap.map_swap). Hence D(v⁽ʲ⁾) + D(v⁽ˡ⁾) = 0.
 Split the sum Φ(v) into the terms i = j, the term i = l, and the rest (Finset.sum_eq_add_of_mem). By (a)–(c), Φ(v) = 0. Together with step 2, Φ is an alternating n-linear form on ℝⁿ.

4. (Reduction to the basis.) Every alternating n-linear form on ℝⁿ is a multiple of the basis determinant: Φ = Φ(e)·e.det (AlternatingMap.eq_smul_basis_det). Evaluate at u and use step 1: Φ(u) = Φ(e)·D(u).

5. (Value at the basis.) Fix i and let c := A(e'_i). Then c = Σ_k c_k e'_k with c_k = e.repr c k (Module.Basis.sum_repr). D is linear in slot i (AlternatingMap.map_update_sum, AlternatingMap.map_update_smul), so
 D(e'⁽ⁱ⁾) = D(Function.update e' i c) = Σ_k c_k·D(Function.update e' i e'_k).
 - For k ≠ i, the tuple Function.update e' i e'_k has the entry e'_k at the two distinct positions i and k, so its D-value is 0.
 - For k = i, the tuple is e' itself, and D(e') = 1.
 Hence D(e'⁽ⁱ⁾) = c_i = (A e'_i)_i, and Φ(e) = Σ_i (A e'_i)_i.
 Correction to the parent's wording: this is also the expansion along row i. Row i of the matrix of Function.update e' i c is (0, …, 0, c_i, 0, …, 0), and deleting row i and column i leaves the identity matrix of size n − 1. The parent's phrase "the other rows are rows of the identity" is not literally true, since those rows carry c_k in column i. The value c_i is unaffected.

6. (Trace.) The matrix B := LinearMap.toMatrix e e A has entries B_{k,i} = e.repr(A(e i)) k = (A e'_i)_k (LinearMap.toMatrix_apply). So Σ_i (A e'_i)_i = Σ_i B_{i,i} = Matrix.trace B = LinearMap.trace ℝ ℝⁿ A, by LinearMap.trace_eq_matrix_trace with the basis e.

7. (Conclusion.) By steps 4–6, Σ_i D(Function.update u i (A(u i))) = Φ(u) = Φ(e)·D(u) = tr(A)·D(u). Written out, this is Σ_i det(Matrix.of fun k j => Function.update u i (A(u i)) j k) = LinearMap.trace ℝ (Euclid n) A · det(Matrix.of fun k j => u j k). The case n = 0 is covered: both sides are 0, since the sum is empty and the trace on the zero space is 0.

Lean note (carried over from the reused node's reviewed proof; its accepted Lean proof, candidate e4813e59, uses the shorter Cramer computation at the end of this note). Steps 1–7 can be formalized with only the frozen imports:
- Let e := (EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin n) ℝ).toBasis. Step 1 is `rw [e.det_apply]; congr 1`.
- Step 2: Φm := ∑ i, (e.det.toMultilinearMap).compLinearMap (f i), with f i j := if j = i then A else LinearMap.id. Its value is computed with the root lemma sum_apply (MultilinearMap.sum_apply is a deprecated alias) and MultilinearMap.compLinearMap_apply.
- Step 3 builds the AlternatingMap { Φm with map_eq_zero_of_eq' := … }. It uses Finset.sum_eq_add_of_mem, e.det.map_eq_zero_of_eq, Function.update_of_ne, Equiv.swap_apply_of_ne_of_ne and e.det.map_swap.
- Step 4 is AlternatingMap.eq_smul_basis_det e Φ, evaluated at u.
- Step 5 uses `conv_lhs => rw [← e.sum_repr (A (e i))]`, AlternatingMap.map_update_sum, Finset.sum_eq_single i, AlternatingMap.map_update_smul, Function.update_eq_self, e.det_self and e.det.map_eq_zero_of_eq.
- Step 6 is LinearMap.trace_eq_matrix_trace ℝ e with Matrix.trace, Matrix.diag_apply and LinearMap.toMatrix_apply.
A shorter computation, also complete and also compiled, may be used instead. Let M := Matrix.of fun k j => u j k and B := LinearMap.toMatrix e e A.
 (i) A(u i) k = (B·M)_{k,i}, by LinearMap.toMatrix_mulVec_repr e e A (u i) and e.repr x = x.
 (ii) Hence the i-th summand is det(M.updateCol i (column i of B·M)).
 (iii) By Cramer's rule this equals (adjugate M ·(B·M))_{i,i} (Matrix.cramer_apply, Matrix.cramer_eq_adjugate_mulVec).
 (iv) Σ_i (adjugate M·(B·M))_{i,i} = trace((B·M)·adjugate M) (Matrix.trace_mul_comm) = trace(B·(det M • 1)) (Matrix.mul_assoc, Matrix.mul_adjugate) = det M·trace B (Matrix.trace_smul), and trace B = tr(A).
proof_key_steps: D(v) := det(Matrix.of fun k j => v j k) equals e.det v for the standard basis e of ℝⁿ (Module.Basis.det_apply, Module.Basis.toMatrix_apply).
Φ(v) := Σ_i D(Function.update v i (A(v i))) is n-linear: each summand is e.det with A in slot i and id in the other slots (compLinearMap).
Φ is alternating. If v j = v l with j ≠ l, the terms i ∉ {j, l} vanish, and the terms i = j and i = l differ by the swap (j l), so they cancel (map_swap).
By linearity in slot i, D(Function.update e i (A e_i)) = (A e_i)_i, so Φ(e) = Σ_i (A e_i)_i = tr(A) (LinearMap.toMatrix_apply, LinearMap.trace_eq_matrix_trace).

subproblems.title: Coordinate trace identity: Σ_i (−1)^i θ(L w_i, w without w_i) = tr(A)·θ(w) for θ = dx^I and p_I∘L = A∘p_I (parent step 3)
subproblems.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ, n := m + 1, I : Fin n → Fin P, and let θ be an n-covector on ℝ^P with θ(v) = det(Matrix.of fun k j => v j (I k)) for every v : Fin n → ℝ^P. Let A : ℝⁿ → ℝⁿ be ℝ-linear, and let L : ℝ^P → ℝ^P be any map with (L v)(I k) = (A(p v))_k for all v ∈ ℝ^P and k ∈ Fin n, where p v := WithLp.toLp 2 (fun k => v (I k)) ∈ ℝⁿ. Then for every w : Fin n → ℝ^P, Σ_{i ∈ Fin n} (−1)^i·θ(Fin.cons (L(w i)) (i.removeNth w)) = tr(A)·θ(w), where tr(A) = LinearMap.trace ℝ ℝⁿ A.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ) (I : Fin (m + 1) → Fin P) (θ : Covector (Euclid P) (m + 1)) (A : Euclid (m + 1) →ₗ[ℝ] Euclid (m + 1)) (L : Euclid P → Euclid P), (∀ v : Fin (m + 1) → Euclid P, θ v = Matrix.det (Matrix.of fun k j => v j (I k))) → (∀ (v : Euclid P) (k : Fin (m + 1)), L v (I k) = A (WithLp.toLp 2 (fun k' => v (I k'))) k) → ∀ w : Fin (m + 1) → Euclid P, ∑ i : Fin (m + 1), (-1 : ℝ) ^ (i : ℕ) * θ (Fin.cons (L (w i)) (i.removeNth w)) = LinearMap.trace ℝ (Euclid (m + 1)) A * θ w
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: the selected parent's proof (node root.dimension_reduction_results-a1.moving_blowups-a1.foundations-a1.divergence_form-a1), step 3 (S_x = tr(Dg(p x))·θ) together with fact (F2). Reuse: this child is the comparator-accepted theorem Submission.cmr_df_cons_sum_trace of DAG node root.compactness_of_minimizing_currents-a1.mass_representation-a1.divergence_form-a1.coordinate_trace-a1 (candidate 342b91b4). It is reused with its byte-identical frozen type, and the reviewed proof of that node is reproduced below. Here L is an arbitrary map in place of DG(x), and A an arbitrary linear map in place of Dg(p x). The parent applies it with A := (fderiv ℝ g (p x)).toLinearMap and L := fderiv ℝ G x = ι ∘ Dg(p x) ∘ p. Then (L v)(I k) = (Dg(p x)(p v))_k, because (ι y)(I k) = y_k.

Notation.
- n := m + 1.
- For v ∈ ℝ^P, p v := WithLp.toLp 2 (fun k => v (I k)) ∈ ℝⁿ, so (p v)_k = v(I k).
- For v : Fin n → ℝⁿ, D(v) := det(Matrix.of fun k j => v j k).
- Fix w : Fin n → ℝ^P and put u_j := p(w j) ∈ ℝⁿ for j ∈ Fin n.

1. (Sign rule; parent fact (F2).) For every i ∈ Fin n and x ∈ ℝ^P,
 (−1)^i·θ(Fin.cons x (i.removeNth w)) = θ(Function.update w i x).
 Proof.
 - Function.update w i x = i.insertNth x (i.removeNth w) (Fin.insertNth_removeNth).
 - For a continuous alternating map, θ(i.insertNth x v) = (−1)^i • θ(Matrix.vecCons x v) (ContinuousAlternatingMap.map_insertNth). The tuple i.insertNth x v comes from Matrix.vecCons x v by moving the entry in position 0 to position i. This is a cyclic permutation of the positions 0, …, i, of sign (−1)^i. (This is the parent's citation of AlternatingMap.map_perm, applied to the underlying alternating map of θ and this cycle. Mathlib packages it for continuous alternating maps as ContinuousAlternatingMap.map_insertNth, Mathlib/Analysis/Normed/Module/Alternating/Uncurry/Fin.lean.)
 - Matrix.vecCons x v is Fin.cons x v by definition. The integer (−1)^i acts on ℝ as multiplication by the real number (−1)^i (zsmul_eq_mul).
 Apply this with x := L(w i):
 (−1)^i·θ(Fin.cons (L(w i)) (i.removeNth w)) = θ(Function.update w i (L(w i))).

2. (Coordinate form of each term.) Fix i. By the hypothesis on θ, θ(Function.update w i (L(w i))) = det N with N_{k,j} := (Function.update w i (L(w i)) j)(I k). Let N' be the matrix of D(Function.update u i (A(u i))), so N'_{k,j} := (Function.update u i (A(u i)) j)_k. We compare entries.
 - If j = i: N_{k,i} = (L(w i))(I k) = (A(p(w i)))_k = (A(u i))_k = N'_{k,i}. This is the hypothesis on L with v := w i.
 - If j ≠ i: N_{k,j} = (w j)(I k) = (p(w j))_k = (u j)_k = N'_{k,j}.
 So N = N', and θ(Function.update w i (L(w i))) = D(Function.update u i (A(u i))).

3. (Jacobi.) Sum steps 1 and 2 over i, and apply the sibling theorem cmr_df_det_update_sum_trace (Jacobi's identity) to n, A and u:
 Σ_i (−1)^i·θ(Fin.cons (L(w i)) (i.removeNth w)) = Σ_i D(Function.update u i (A(u i))) = tr(A)·D(u).

4. (Back to θ.) By the hypothesis on θ, D(u) = det(Matrix.of fun k j => (u j)_k) = det(Matrix.of fun k j => w j (I k)) = θ(w). So the sum equals tr(A)·θ(w) = LinearMap.trace ℝ (Euclid (m+1)) A · θ(w).

Remarks.
- (i) The proof does not use that I is injective or monotone.
- (ii) Lean route (compiled). Step 1: `rw [← Fin.insertNth_removeNth, ContinuousAlternatingMap.map_insertNth]`, then `zsmul_eq_mul` with `push_cast`, then `rfl`, since Matrix.vecCons = Fin.cons. Step 2: `rw [hθ]; congr 1; ext k j`, then `by_cases hj : j = i` with `simp [hL]`. Finally `simp_rw` the two steps, `rw` the sibling theorem, and finish with `hθ`.
proof_key_steps: (−1)^i·θ(Fin.cons (L(w i)) (i.removeNth w)) = θ(Function.update w i (L(w i))), by Fin.insertNth_removeNth and ContinuousAlternatingMap.map_insertNth.
With u_j := p_I(w j), the hypothesis (L v)(I k) = (A(p_I v))_k gives θ(Function.update w i (L(w i))) = D(Function.update u i (A(u i))), entry by entry.
Jacobi's identity (sibling cmr_df_det_update_sum_trace) gives Σ_i D(Function.update u i (A(u i))) = tr(A)·D(u).
D(u) = θ(w), by the formula for θ.

subproblems.title: Exterior derivative of b·(θ contracted with a vector field G) (parent step 2)
subproblems.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ, let θ be an (m+1)-covector on ℝ^P, let b : ℝ^P → ℝ and G : ℝ^P → ℝ^P, and let x ∈ ℝ^P be a point where b and G are differentiable. Let η be the m-form η(y) := b(y)•θ.curryLeft(G y), i.e. η(y)(v) = b(y)·θ(Fin.cons (G y) v). Then for every w : Fin (m+1) → ℝ^P the exterior derivative (exteriorDerivative) satisfies dη(x)(w) = Σ_{i ∈ Fin (m+1)} (−1)^i·[Db(x)(w i)·θ(Fin.cons (G x) (i.removeNth w)) + b(x)·θ(Fin.cons (DG(x)(w i)) (i.removeNth w))].
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ) (θ : Covector (Euclid P) (m + 1)) (b : Euclid P → ℝ) (G : Euclid P → Euclid P) (x : Euclid P), DifferentiableAt ℝ b x → DifferentiableAt ℝ G x → ∀ w : Fin (m + 1) → Euclid P, exteriorDerivative (fun y => b y • ContinuousAlternatingMap.curryLeft θ (G y)) x w = ∑ i : Fin (m + 1), (-1 : ℝ) ^ (i : ℕ) * (fderiv ℝ b x (w i) * θ (Fin.cons (G x) (i.removeNth w)) + b x * θ (Fin.cons (fderiv ℝ G x (w i)) (i.removeNth w)))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: the selected parent's proof (node root.dimension_reduction_results-a1.moving_blowups-a1.foundations-a1.divergence_form-a1), step 2 (derivative of η). Reuse: this child is the comparator-accepted theorem Submission.cmr_df_extDeriv_smul_curryLeft of DAG node root.compactness_of_minimizing_currents-a1.mass_representation-a1.divergence_form-a1.contraction_extderiv-a1 (candidate c9a1cfd3). It is reused with its byte-identical frozen type, and the reviewed proof of that node is reproduced below. Here b and G are arbitrary maps that are differentiable at the point x. The parent applies it at every x with G := ι ∘ g ∘ p, which is C^∞.

Notation.
- C := θ.curryLeft = ContinuousAlternatingMap.curryLeft θ : ℝ^P →L[ℝ] Covector(ℝ^P, m). This is a continuous linear map, and C(u)(v) = θ(Matrix.vecCons u v) = θ(Fin.cons u v) for u ∈ ℝ^P and v : Fin m → ℝ^P (ContinuousAlternatingMap.curryLeft_apply_apply).
- η(y) := b(y)•C(G y) ∈ Covector(ℝ^P, m).
- Fix w : Fin (m+1) → ℝ^P.

1. (Derivative of η.) The map y ↦ C(G y) is differentiable at x with derivative C ∘L DG(x). This is the chain rule for the continuous linear map C, whose derivative is C itself (ContinuousLinearMap.fderiv, fderiv_fun_comp). By the product rule for a scalar function times a vector-valued function (fderiv_fun_smul), η is differentiable at x, and for all h ∈ ℝ^P:
 Dη(x)h = b(x)•C(DG(x)h) + Db(x)h•C(G x).

2. (Exterior derivative formula.) η is differentiable at x, so the exterior derivative formula (Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter06.exteriorDerivative_apply) gives
 dη(x)(w) = Σ_{i ∈ Fin (m+1)} (−1)^i • D_x[y ↦ η(y)(i.removeNth w)](w i).
 Here (−1)^i is an integer acting on ℝ.

3. (Differentiating an evaluation.) Fix a tuple v : Fin m → ℝ^P. Evaluation at v is a continuous linear map on m-covectors (ContinuousAlternatingMap.apply). So y ↦ η(y)(v) is differentiable at x, and D_x[y ↦ η(y)(v)](h) = (Dη(x)h)(v) for all h (fderiv_continuousAlternatingMap_apply_const_apply).

4. (Evaluating the derivative.) By steps 1 and 3 and the formula for C:
 D_x[y ↦ η(y)(v)](h) = b(x)·θ(Fin.cons (DG(x)h) v) + Db(x)h·θ(Fin.cons (G x) v).

5. (Conclusion.) Take h := w i and v := i.removeNth w in step 4, and substitute into step 2. Write the integer (−1)^i as the real number (−1)^i (zsmul_eq_mul) and reorder the two summands. This gives
 dη(x)(w) = Σ_i (−1)^i·[Db(x)(w i)·θ(Fin.cons (G x) (i.removeNth w)) + b(x)·θ(Fin.cons (DG(x)(w i)) (i.removeNth w))],
 which is the claim.

Lean route (compiled, about 25 lines).
- Differentiability: hη := hb.smul ((ContinuousAlternatingMap.curryLeft θ).differentiableAt.comp x hG).
- `rw [exteriorDerivative_apply hη w]`, then Finset.sum_congr rfl, then `rw [fderiv_continuousAlternatingMap_apply_const_apply hη]`.
- Rewrite fderiv ℝ η x using fderiv_fun_smul hb hc, fderiv_fun_comp x (ContinuousAlternatingMap.curryLeft θ).differentiableAt hG, and ContinuousLinearMap.fderiv.
- Finish with `simp only` using the root lemmas add_apply and smul_apply (ContinuousLinearMap.add_apply and ContinuousLinearMap.smul_apply are deprecated aliases), ContinuousLinearMap.coe_comp, Function.comp_apply, ContinuousLinearMap.smulRight_apply, ContinuousAlternatingMap.add_apply, ContinuousAlternatingMap.smul_apply, ContinuousAlternatingMap.curryLeft_apply_apply, smul_eq_mul and zsmul_eq_mul. Then `simp only [Matrix.vecCons]`, `push_cast` and `ring`.
proof_key_steps: η = b•(θ.curryLeft ∘ G) is differentiable at x, with Dη(x)h = b(x)•θ.curryLeft(DG(x)h) + Db(x)h•θ.curryLeft(G x) (chain rule for the CLM θ.curryLeft, product rule).
exteriorDerivative_apply: dη(x)(w) = Σ_i (−1)^i D_x[η(·)(i.removeNth w)](w i).
Differentiation commutes with evaluation at a fixed tuple (fderiv_continuousAlternatingMap_apply_const_apply), and θ.curryLeft u v = θ(Fin.cons u v). Substitute h = w i and v = i.removeNth w.

subproblems.title: The Euclidean coefficient norm of n-covectors is a continuous seminorm dominated by the operator norm
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let F := Covector (Euclid P) n (continuous alternating n-linear forms on ℝ^P with the operator norm ‖·‖), and let N := covectorEuclideanNorm, i.e. N(α) = (Σ_{I : Fin n → Fin P strictly increasing} α(e_{I(0)}, …, e_{I(n−1)})²)^{1/2} for the standard orthonormal basis (e_j) of ℝ^P. Then (i) N(α + α') ≤ N(α) + N(α') for all α, α' ∈ F; (ii) N(t·α) = |t|·N(α) for all t ∈ ℝ and α ∈ F; (iii) there is a real C ≥ 0 with N(α) ≤ C·‖α‖ for all α ∈ F; and (iv) N : F → ℝ is continuous.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ), (∀ α α' : Covector (Euclid P) n, covectorEuclideanNorm (α + α') ≤ covectorEuclideanNorm α + covectorEuclideanNorm α') ∧ (∀ (t : ℝ) (α : Covector (Euclid P) n), covectorEuclideanNorm (t • α) = |t| * covectorEuclideanNorm α) ∧ (∃ C : ℝ, 0 ≤ C ∧ ∀ α : Covector (Euclid P) n, covectorEuclideanNorm α ≤ C * ‖α‖) ∧ Continuous (fun α : Covector (Euclid P) n => covectorEuclideanNorm α)
subproblems.natural_proof:
This is the comparator-accepted theorem of DAG node root.regular_set_dense-a1.mass_eq_weight-a1.test_form_approx-a1.norm_props-a1 (candidate f492ba4a). It is reused with its identical frozen type, and its accepted proof is reproduced below. In the parent it supplies fact (F1): part (iii) with n = m and with n = m + 1 gives constants C_m, C_n ≥ 0, depending only on P and the degree, with covectorEuclideanNorm α ≤ C_k‖α‖. The proof below gives C_k = √(card(Fin k → Fin P)) = √(P^k) ≤ P^k, which is at least as good as the parent's constant P^k.

Notation.
- e_j := EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ j (j ∈ Fin P) is the standard orthonormal basis of ℝ^P, so ‖e_j‖ = 1.
- 𝓙 is the finite type of all maps I : Fin n → Fin P, and #𝓙 = Fintype.card (Fin n → Fin P).
- For I ∈ 𝓙, e_I := (e_{I(0)}, …, e_{I(n−1)}), in Lean (fun i => e (I i)).
- F := Covector (Euclid P) n carries the operator norm ‖·‖ of continuous alternating maps.
- By definition N(α) := covectorEuclideanNorm α = √(Σ_{I∈𝓙} q_I(α)), where q_I(α) := α(e_I)² if I is strictly increasing and q_I(α) := 0 otherwise.

1. (Coefficient vector.) For α ∈ F and I ∈ 𝓙 put c_I(α) := α(e_I) if I is strictly increasing, and c_I(α) := 0 otherwise. Since (if p then a else 0)² = (if p then a² else 0), q_I(α) = c_I(α)² for every I. Let v(α) ∈ EuclideanSpace ℝ 𝓙 be the vector with coordinates c_I(α); in Lean, v α := WithLp.toLp 2 (fun I => c_I α). The Euclidean norm formula ‖w‖ = √(Σ_I ‖w_I‖²) (EuclideanSpace.norm_eq) and ‖w_I‖² = w_I² give
 N(α) = ‖v(α)‖ for every α ∈ F. (∗)

2. (Linearity of v.) Evaluation at a fixed tuple is linear in the form: (α + α')(e_I) = α(e_I) + α'(e_I) and (t·α)(e_I) = t·α(e_I). So c_I(α + α') = c_I(α) + c_I(α') and c_I(t·α) = t·c_I(α) for every I; both sides are 0 when I is not strictly increasing. Hence v(α + α') = v(α) + v(α') and v(t·α) = t·v(α) (WithLp.toLp_add, WithLp.toLp_smul).

3. (Proof of (i).) By (∗), step 2 and the triangle inequality in EuclideanSpace ℝ 𝓙:
 N(α + α') = ‖v(α) + v(α')‖ ≤ ‖v(α)‖ + ‖v(α')‖ = N(α) + N(α').

4. (Proof of (ii).) By (∗), step 2 and homogeneity of the norm:
 N(t·α) = ‖t·v(α)‖ = |t|·‖v(α)‖ = |t|·N(α).

5. (Coordinate bound.) For every I ∈ 𝓙, |c_I(α)| ≤ ‖α‖.
 - If I is strictly increasing, the operator-norm bound for continuous alternating maps (ContinuousAlternatingMap.le_opNorm) gives |α(e_I)| ≤ ‖α‖·∏_k ‖e_{I(k)}‖ = ‖α‖·1 = ‖α‖.
 - Otherwise |c_I(α)| = 0 ≤ ‖α‖.

6. (Proof of (iii).) Put C := √(#𝓙) ≥ 0. By step 5, c_I(α)² = |c_I(α)|² ≤ ‖α‖² for every I, so Σ_I c_I(α)² ≤ #𝓙·‖α‖². Since √ is monotone and ‖α‖ ≥ 0,
 N(α) = √(Σ_I c_I(α)²) ≤ √(#𝓙·‖α‖²) = √(#𝓙)·√(‖α‖²) = C·‖α‖.

7. (Proof of (iv).) Let α, α' ∈ F.
 - By (i), N(α) = N((α − α') + α') ≤ N(α − α') + N(α').
 - α' − α = −(α − α'), and N(−β) = N(β) (covectorEuclideanNorm_neg, or (ii) with t = −1). So by (i), N(α') = N((α' − α) + α) ≤ N(α' − α) + N(α) = N(α − α') + N(α).
 With (iii), |N(α) − N(α')| ≤ N(α − α') ≤ C·‖α − α'‖. So dist(N(α), N(α')) ≤ C·dist(α, α') for all α, α'. Hence N is Lipschitz with the nonnegative constant C (LipschitzWith.of_dist_le_mul with K := ⟨C, C ≥ 0⟩), and therefore continuous.

Steps 3, 4, 6 and 7 prove (i)–(iv), with the constant C of (iii) equal to √(Fintype.card (Fin n → Fin P)).
proof_key_steps: Write N(α) = ‖v(α)‖ for the coefficient vector v(α) := (α(e_I) if I is strictly increasing, else 0)_I in EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n → Fin P).
v is additive and ℝ-homogeneous, because evaluation at a fixed tuple is linear in α.
(i) and (ii) follow from the triangle inequality and homogeneity of the Euclidean norm.
|α(e_I)| ≤ ‖α‖·∏‖e_{I(k)}‖ = ‖α‖, so N(α) ≤ √(card(Fin n → Fin P))·‖α‖. This is (iii).
|N(α) − N(α')| ≤ N(α − α') ≤ C‖α − α'‖, so N is Lipschitz and hence continuous. This is (iv).
